title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
gist: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Pinterest's Jordan Cutler argued AI changes where a staff engineer's leverage lies: internal Pinterest data shows the top 10% of engineers increased merged PRs 68% while the bottom half gained only 14%. His team encoded repeated judgment into shared agent tooling and built a scheduled, sandboxed agent system for migrations, yielding about 4x output per engineer versus other web teams using the same AI tools.

insights.claim: Internal Pinterest data from Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 shows the top 10% of engineers rose from 6.7 to 11.3 merged PRs per week (+68%), while the bottom half rose only from 1.0 to 1.15 (+14%).
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: AI tools amplify dispersion in engineer productivity rather than leveling it, so enterprise AI ROI depends heavily on adoption practices, not license counts.
insights.locator: To illustrate why this matters, Cutler shared

insights.claim: When every engineer has access to the same AI tools, the gap in output between engineers keeps growing because not everyone uses AI the same way.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Vendors selling enablement, workflow encoding and adoption tooling may capture value beyond raw model access.
insights.quote: Everyone has AI, but not everyone uses it the same way, and the gap keeps growing.

insights.claim: Cutler's team at Pinterest ships about four times as much per engineer as other Pinterest web teams using the same AI tools, excluding his own PRs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Organizational design around AI, not tool choice, may be the main driver of engineering productivity differences.

insights.claim: AI did not change what a staff engineer is for but changed where the leverage is: from personal output toward encoding judgment into tools, defaults and systems used across the organization.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Expect demand for platforms that capture and distribute team conventions to AI agents (shared prompts, rules, review bots).

insights.claim: Encoding repeated code-review corrections and conventions for AI agents grows in value with every teammate who adopts it, versus the flat value curve of a single engineer working alone.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Network-effect dynamics inside teams favor shared agent configuration over individual tool use.
insights.locator: The second move, multiply your team

insights.claim: Staff engineers should try new AI tools before their teams and share dead ends early, such as agent harnesses that cannot be steered mid-task or remote agent runners needing too many follow-ups, to save the team weeks of duplicated experimentation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Steerability and low follow-up overhead are practical purchase criteria for agent tooling.

insights.claim: Pinterest built a system where a staff engineer supplies a plan and example, an engineer schedules it, and a sandboxed agent splits a codebase-wide migration into PRs team by team; a class component migration ran three to five times faster than by hand.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Large-scale code migrations are a concrete, high-ROI enterprise use case for background coding agents.
insights.locator: The third move, multiply the system

insights.claim: Like the shipping container cut cargo handling cost from $5.86 to 16 cents a ton, standardizing how repetitive code changes are executed by agents changes software economics more than speeding up manual work.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: System-level standardization of agent workflows is where step-change efficiency gains lie.

insights.claim: A looping scheduled agent job at Pinterest opened 16 PRs in two minutes and pushed CI wait times from under 30 seconds to 14 minutes, showing autonomous agents can stress shared CI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Agent adoption increases load on CI and requires guardrails; a demand driver for CI capacity and agent-governance tooling.
insights.locator: The talk also covered what went wrong.

insights.claim: At Pinterest, 40 engineers now run their own agent scheduler jobs, with suggested 'any' use cases such as first responders for any incident, draft fixes for any bug ticket, or triage of any flaky test.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Background/scheduled agents are spreading bottom-up inside large engineering orgs.
